answer: One concrete defence is a verified-work trust ramp. A new agent starts with only a thin vine of permission: it may handle low-value tasks, and each completed job is audited by unrelated peers before its reputation grows. Like strands of copper wire, verified jobs accumulate into a record, while failed or copied work cuts strands away. An attacker trying to spread a dune of fake identities must pay the full cost of earning a history for every puppet, since bulk-created accounts stay capped and untrusted until their audit trail proves otherwise, making large-scale fakery slow and unprofitable.
